A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPHNet and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPHNet experiments on QH9, PubChemQH and MD17, alongside sparsity, scheduler, architecture and scaling analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original benchmark results and adds experiments applying sparse gates to QHNet and varying SPHNet block counts.

M1.justification: The central SPHNet architecture, loss and scheduler remain intact. Section 5.7 adds a concrete QHNet adaptation, inserting pair gating into its second non-diagonal block and TP gating into interaction and pair blocks. Equation 6 also revises the inner-product superscript from 0 to 1:, without establishing whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four MD17 molecules, QH9, PubChemQH and six PubChemQC PM6 molecules for size-scaling tests. The added analyses do not introduce new datasets, tasks or molecular environments.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical split-specific comparator membership: QHNet and WANet where reported, and SchNOrb, PhiSNet and QHNet on MD17. New Table 6 evaluates ablations of the proposed gates within QHNet. Newly discussed E2Former and DEHQ are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The architectural ablation design changes: v1 replaces vectorial blocks with additional spherical blocks, whereas v2 disables both gates and separately reduces vectorial, spherical or pair-construction block counts to one. The QHNet transfer experiment introduces additional gating configurations. Existing benchmark splits, budgets, metrics and sparsity-sweep settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends component validation through the QHNet gate-transfer experiment, separate block-count ablations, and fuller speed/memory analysis across sparsity rates (Tables 6, 8 and 9). The earlier vectorial-to-spherical replacement analysis is removed. Scheduler and SPHNet gate ablations are retained and moved into Section 5.7, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs for the scheduler ablations and retain the same means and dispersion values. No new seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests appear. The missing ± before 1.33 in v2 Table 4 is a formatting defect, not evidence of a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically identical. Added Table 6 reports doubly gated versus ungated QHNet at 1.45 versus 0.44 samples/s, 8.46 versus 22.50 GB/sample, and Hamiltonian MAE 128.89 versus 123.74 in units of 10^-6 Eh. Tables 8–9 add block-count outcomes and fuller resource measurements. The earlier replacement configuration's MAE 97.08 and efficiency results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the matrix dimensions accompanying Equation 1 and adds Appendix D.7's computational-complexity accounting: O(|U|) random selection, O(|U| log |U|) adaptive selection and O(L^3) TP-gate weighting. Existing tensor-product and spherical-harmonic derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: two adaptive sparse gates, a three-phase scheduler, efficient Hamiltonian prediction and potential applicability to other equivariant networks. The headline accuracy, approximately sevenfold speedup and memory-saving claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the QHNet experiment as evidence of gate transferability and the block-count tests as support for progressively increasing representation order. It also identifies possible further acceleration by removing a pair-construction block. The earlier interpretation of the vectorial-to-spherical efficiency comparison disappears; existing molecular-size and long-range-interaction interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository address in the abstract, supplementing v1's statement that code accompanies the supplementary material. It also specifies gate insertion locations for the QHNet adaptation. Existing software versions, hardware, training schedules, loss and residual-target implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix E adds discussion and citations for E2Former and DEHQ, and expands the account of WANet's wavefunction-alignment loss. WANet was already cited and evaluated in v1. Other reference changes principally update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Scheduler and gate ablations are rewritten and promoted from Appendix B into new Section 5.7, while appendix subsections are reorganized. Local wording, headings, author order and publication information are edited, and an impact statement is added. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The retained scheduler and gate tables are transposed and moved into the main text, and tables are added or replaced for the new analyses. All nine figure images are reused; Figures 2–5 are enlarged, and appendix figures are relocated and renumbered. These are localized display changes.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the previously prospective transferability argument with a QHNet experiment and provides more controlled block-count comparisons, fuller sparsity-cost reporting, complexity analysis and clearer code access. These improve evidential support and reproducibility while leaving the main benchmark findings unchanged. Losing the earlier block-replacement efficiency analysis and introducing a small uncertainty-formatting defect temper, but do not outweigh, these gains.
